[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cycle World is a magazine and does not offer in-person classes, but has online resources including articles, videos, and tutorials on bike maintenance and repair.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common issues that can cause a rear derailleur to make strange noises include misalignment, worn or damaged pulleys, chain wear or stretch, dirty or corroded components, incorrect derailleur adjustment, chain skipping, cassette wear, and derailleur pivot friction.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To troubleshoot the rear derailleur issue, the user can inspect the derailleur, pulleys, and cassette for signs of wear or damage, clean the components, check the chain for wear, adjust the derailleur's limit screws, and lubricate the pivot points.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To check the derailleur hanger for misalignment, the user should shift the chain to the smallest cog, visually inspect the hanger for bending, use a hanger alignment tool, and check the derailleur's position relative to the cassette.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To adjust the limit screws, the user should shift the chain to the smallest cog, locate the limit screws, turn them clockwise to tighten, shift to the largest cog, check the chain's alignment, and make small adjustments as needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To inspect the cassette, the user should remove the rear wheel, visually inspect for worn-out teeth, corrosion, and grime, and check the splines for wear.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To clean the cassette, the user should soak it in a solvent, use a soft-bristled brush to scrub it, rinse it with clean water, dry it, and apply lubricant.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The average cassette can last for around 5,000 to 10,000 miles, depending on riding conditions and maintenance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should consider replacing their cassette every 5,000 to 7,000 miles or every 2-3 years, depending on riding frequency and conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Signs of a worn-out cassette include worn-out teeth, corrosion, excessive wear on the splines, difficulty shifting, and chain skipping.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The mechanic will be able to diagnose the rear derailleur issue and may be able to adjust, repair, or replace it depending on the extent of the damage or wear.
